html:
A huge hydroelectric dam on the Yangtze River in Hubei, central China, the largest power station in the world by capacity. Building began in 1994, the dam wall was finished in 2006, and the last generators came online in 2012.

The idea was old: Sun Yat-sen proposed a dam at the Three Gorges in 1919. The project was meant to make clean electricity, control the floods that had killed hundreds of thousands along the Yangtze, and let large ships reach Chongqing.

Its reservoir stretches about 600 km upstream. It drowned towns, farmland and old sites, and more than a million people were moved. Critics point to landslides, trapped silt and harm to river life; the Yangtze river dolphin was declared probably extinct in 2006. The dam is a symbol of China's state-led building boom after reform and opening, along with the high-speed railways. Other giant dams of the age include India's Bhakra Dam and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam.
